findings.issue: The consumer-facing Minkowski statements use raw coordinate access `v (Sum.inl 0)` instead of Physlib's accessor `Lorentz.Vector.timeComponent`, which is the idiom everywhere else in this repo. Affects `minkowskiAxis_plus_apply` (400), `minkowskiAxis_minus_apply` (407), `mem_transverse_minkowskiAxis_iff` (415), and the private helpers `minkowskiProduct_axisVector_left` (349), `axisVector_apply_inl` (356). findings.issue: `bilinForm_nPlus_right_eq_zero_of_mem_transverse` (279) and `bilinForm_nMinus_right_eq_zero_of_mem_transverse` (285) are nothing but `.1` and `.2` of `mem_transverse_iff_bilinForm_right_eq_zero` (272) stated three lines above, and are used only inside this file (lines 296-298). summary: No existing declaration is duplicated outright: Mathlib has no hyperbolic/light-cone pair, and the Mathlib orthogonal-complement results that come closest all carry hypotheses this PR does not assume. Three reuse gaps remain: the Minkowski statements bypass Physlib's `timeComponent` accessor, `mem_transverse_iff` re-derives `Submodule.mem_orthogonalBilin_span`, and two public lemmas are `.1`/`.2` projections of the iff next to them.
